articles.title: World Cup 2026: Germany 2-1 Ivory Coast - Deniz Undav scores 94th-minute winner in Group E clash
articles.summary: Match report as Germany reach the World Cup knockout stages with a late 2-1 win over Ivory Coast in Group E; Deniz Undav scored twice from the bench with his winner coming in the 94th minute; Franck Kessie opened the scoring for Ivory Coast
articles.body:
Deniz Undav's 94th-minute goal clinched a come-from-behind 2-1 victory for Germany against Ivory Coast in Group E to send them into the World Cup knockout stages.

Substitute Undav clinically dispatched the winner from Felix Nmecha's pass having earlier cancelled out Ivory Coast captain Franck Kessie's opener by volleying in a Nadiem Amiri cross.

Germany appeared to be heading for a shock defeat before the former Brighton striker's 60th-minute introduction but his goals, which put him on nine in 11 games for his country, mean they join USA and Mexico in reaching the knockouts with a game to spare.

  • As it happened | Teams | Stats | Group E guide
  • World Cup day-by-day schedule | Latest: World Cup
  • Follow our World Cup coverage in the Sky Sports App

Ivory Coast, winners against Ecuador in their opener, were the better side in the first half, inspired by Liverpool target Yan Diomande, who helped set up Kessie's goal with a burst of pace and low cross, but the defeat means they still have work to do to qualify.

The key moments from Toronto...

  • 10: SAVE! Yahia Fofana makes a good save to stop Kai Havertz's header
  • 22: GOAL RULED OUT! Aleksandar Pavlovic forces a corner over the line but is penalised for a foul on the goalkeeper
  • 30: GOAL! Diomande's wicked low cross allows Kessie to score
  • 39: GOAL RULED OUT! Germany denied again after Havertz's goal is chalked off for a foul by Jamal Musiala
  • 60: Germany introduce Undav as part of a triple change
  • 68: GOAL! Undav volleys in Amiri's excellent centre to level it up
  • 90+4: GOAL! Undav dispatches the winner to spark wild Germany celebrations

In pictures: Undav's match-winning moment

Analysis: Undav an ace up Germany's sleeve?

Deniz Undav did not make much of a mark in the Premier League, scoring a modest total of five goals in 22 appearances for Brighton during the 2022/23 season. But his match-winning double against Ivory Coast follows a goal and two assists against Curacao.

His impact should come as no surprise.

The 29-year-old came into the tournament on the back of an impressive campaign for Stuttgart which featured 25 goals in 46 games in all competitions and his international scoring record is even more impressive, especially as he usually features from the bench.

He is a late bloomer. He only made his senior international debut two years ago at the age of 27. But in a squad which features more illustrious names, he is showing himself to be Germany's real difference-maker with an early push for the Golden Boot.

Neville: This is what Germany do

Gary Neville told ITV: "In the first 10 or 15 minutes of the second half, Ivory Coast should have killed the game off.

"But it's just what Germany do. They've ruined my life on multiple occasions.

"You've got to hand it to Germany there. They were struggling in parts of that match.

"They stuck at it, persistence, resilience and they got there in the end. It's so Germany."

What the result means...

articles.title: Iranian dad helps blind son feel the World Cup | CNN
articles.summary: Ardeshir and his nine-year-old visually impaired son Alireza have gone viral because of how Ardeshir helps him experience football games. Using a carboard map of a soccer field and his finger, he helps his son visualize what’s going on.
articles.body:
Ardeshir and his nine-year-old visually impaired son Alireza have gone viral because of how Ardeshir helps him experience football games. Using a cardboard map of a soccer field and his finger, he helps his son visualize what’s going on.

Videos showing a person dressed up as Cat in the Hat roaming streets after dark have spread across social media, even prompting responses from police in Ireland and the UK. But it remains unclear which, if any, of the sightings are real or if they are AI-generated.

Kirk Heilbrun, a psychologist called by the prosecution , testified that he concluded Lindsay Clancy was not psychotic when she killed her three children and understood her actions were wrong. Helibrun told the court his "clinical opinion is that she was criminally responsible on January 24th." Defense attorneys for Clancy, who is charged with murder, argue she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and extreme mental illness and should not be held criminally responsible for the killings.

Justin Lester, a pastor in Vallejo, California created an "AI twin" so his constituents could have access to him 24/7. CNN's Nick Watt speaks to him about how it works.

Target is facing backlash for selling a children’s Halloween costume depicting a circus clown that critics said evoked blackface and minstrel shows. The company announced it pulled the item and acknowledged the issue in an apology.

Natalie Harp’s now-inactive Twitter feed shows a non-stop thread of posts showing devotion to President Donald Trump. These posts were on her account years before she became a White House aide to the president, posting more than 150 tweets on January 6, 2021, alone, in support of the president. CNN's Isabelle Chapman reports.

Capybaras, penguins and even giant snails were weighed and measured as London Zoo carried out its annual health checks. The data helps keep track of the animals’ health and contributes to a global conservation database.

Divine, a new app inspired by six-second video platform Vine, launched last week and already has about 100,000 users, according to its founder. CNN’s Matias Grez looks at what you can do on the app and how it stands apart from other mainstream social media platforms. Divine is not formally affiliated with Vine.

articles.summary: Hours ahead of a consequential World Cup knockout match, FIFA has denied Belgium’s ability to appeal the overturned decision on US striker Folarin Balogun’s red card. CNN’s Coy Wire reports

articles.title: Jurgen Klopp: Former Liverpool boss on the verge of becoming Germany head coach and replacing Julian Nagelsmann
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp had shown a "general willingness" to take the role; Julian Nagelsmann departed after Germany's World Cup exit; Nagelsmann had been in charge of Germany since September 2023
articles.body:
Jurgen Klopp is on the verge of becoming Germany's new head coach after reaching an agreement in principle with the German Football Association [DFB], according to reports in Germany.

A breakthrough was made during negotiations in New York on Friday, reports Sky in Germany, with Klopp expected to sign a contract running until the end of the 2030 World Cup. Only the final details remain to be resolved.

Klopp's departure from his role at Red Bull is expected to be finalised with the company's chief executive Oliver Mintzlaff in New York by early next week.

The DFB are planning to announce the agreement on Saturday.

The former Liverpool boss was head of global soccer for Red Bull Group, but his contract included a special exit clause for the Germany job.

  • Germany were once World Cup kings. Now they're simply not that good
  • World Cup day-by-day schedule | Latest: World Cup
  • Follow our World Cup coverage in the Sky Sports App

It is Klopp's first coaching job since leaving Liverpool in 2024.

Nagelsmann stepped down from the role after Germany's shock World Cup last-32 exit against Paraguay.

The 38-year-old took charge of Germany in September 2023 and guided the nation to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were beaten by eventual winners Spain.

articles.summary: FIFA’s proposed plan to sell private stakes in upcoming World Cup tournaments that sparked backlash from fans and soccer associations around the world has been scrapped, FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement.
articles.body:
FIFA’s proposed plan to sell private stakes in upcoming World Cup tournaments that sparked backlash from fans and soccer associations around the world has been scrapped, FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement.

Kirk Heilbrun, a psychologist called by the prosecution , testified that he concluded Lindsay Clancy was not psychotic when she killed her three children and understood her actions were wrong. Helibrun told the court his "clinical opinion is that she was criminally responsible on January 24th." Defense attorneys for Clancy, who is charged with murder, argue she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and extreme mental illness and should not be held criminally responsible for the killings.

The family of Alex Pretti says they’re still searching for answers seven months after federal immigration agents in Minneapolis shot and killed the 37-year-old in January. In an interview on ABC’s “Good Morning America,” Pretti’s father called President Donald Trump “unpresidential” over his response to the killing, as the family says they haven’t heard anything from Trump administration officials about the incident. CNN is reaching out to the White House for comment.

A video aired by Iran’s state broadcaster appeared to threaten the life of Barron Trump, the youngest son of President Donald Trump. The nearly three-minute video features stylized graphics and shows locations where the younger Trump is publicly known to spend time. CNN’s Alayna Treene reports from the White House.

Escorted by Israeli soldiers, far-right Israeli lawmaker smashed a memorial in a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank. The military says Sukkot violated the approved plan for the trip, but the firebrand politician had vowed one week before to destroy the memorial.

The Trump administration has quietly struck deportation deals with at least 35 nations, often worth millions, according to Third Country Deportation. Isobel Yeung investigates where the money is going and what happens to migrants sent to a country they’ve never been to.

Two fast-growing fires have hit North and Central Texas, with evacuations issued. No injuries have yet to be reported.

Target is facing backlash for selling a children’s Halloween costume depicting a circus clown that critics said evoked blackface and minstrel shows. The company announced it pulled the item and acknowledged the issue in an apology.

articles.title: Premier League summer transfer window: What your club still needs to do in the week before Deadline Day
articles.summary: We are entering the final week of the Premier League transfer window and nearly every club is still active in the market ahead of the Tuesday September 1 deadline; Follow every twist and turn with our dedicated Transfer Centre blog and on Sky Sports News
articles.body:
Arsenal

Arsenal will not give up on the signing of Julian Alvarez right until the end but, with his heart set on a move to Barcelona and Atletico refusing to sell to them, it still looks unlikely to happen at this stage.

Everyone is waiting to see if Alvarez changes his stance and opens up to the idea, but if he doesn't, Arsenal are happy with their squad and won't just pivot to any other forward. They want top quality only.

Meanwhile, Al Hilal are trying to sign Gabriel Martinelli and the player is understood to be seriously considering a move to Saudi. Ethan Nwaneri could depart on loan while Arsenal are understood to be willing to listen to offers for Gabriel Jesus.

Mikel Arteta has ruled out the possibility of Myles Lewis-Skelly or Martin Zubimendi leaving.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Papers - latest headlines
  • Premier League done deals | Key dates for summer window
  • Download the Sky Sports app and follow your club

Aston Villa

Aston Villa face a busy final week with more potential ins and outs in a summer of upheaval. They are working on forward options, a new midfielder and a replacement for Ezri Konsa at the back.

Most recently, they have made approaches for forwards Jean Philippe Mateta and Raphael Leao and have been in talks for defenders Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Joel Ordonez.

With Amadou Onana out and now new signing Joao Gomes suspended, Villa are close to signing free agent Leon Goretzka to strengthen the midfield.

Up front, Nicolas Jackson at Chelsea is also another option if they lose Ollie Watkins to Al Hilal.

Emi Martinez's future is still uncertain after Villa signed Zion Suzuki in goal before the Argentina star had found another club to go to.

Bournemouth

Bournemouth are expecting the signing of Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio to be their final transfer of the summer. He has joined on a season-long loan which includes an option to buy at £12m.

As ever, Bournemouth are still open to a market opportunity should one arise in the final days of the window.

There is a possibility that their resolve is tested by a big bid for Alex Scott from one of either Chelsea or Manchester City, depending on what happens with Enzo Fernandez's future.

However, Bournemouth do not want to sell and insist they are under no pressure to do so. The midfielder has two years left on his current deal but has turned down the club's offer of a new one.

Brentford

Brentford are very happy with their squad and rightly so; they took Spurs to task on the opening day with a resounding 3-0 win.

The only area of the side they are still looking at is on the left, but only if they can be assured to add more quality; ergo market opportunities only. There is some flexibility on the profile too; it could be a left-back or left-winger.

They have been keen on West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf, who is primarily a left-back, which would allow Keane Lewis-Potter to operate further forward more regularly. But he is one of four left-back options at the club including Rico Henry, Jayden Meghoma and Aaron Hickey, so they are not desperate.

Meghoma could be one of several who go on loan.

Brighton

Brighton have work to do with Yankuba Minteh attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Carlos Baleba joining Manchester United.

They are working on a deal for BSC Young Boys left-back Jaouen Hadjam with Maxim De Cuyper starting the season playing further forward.

Brighton are also exploring a potential deal for Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez but face competition from Hull City among others.

They could also sign another midfielder, with Baleba - and potentially Matt O'Riley - leaving. O'Reilly has interest from Lyon and other top European clubs having recovered from an illness.

Brighton would consider offers for Evan Ferguson and Igor Julio if they arrive.

Chelsea

The only first-team position that could see a change in is midfield. Manchester City are interested in Enzo Fernandez and, if he leaves, Alex Scott and Adam Wharton are among the players Chelsea are expected to have a serious look at.

The remaining business will be all outgoings, with as many as nine players leaving Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa are expected to move for Nicolas Jackson if Ollie Watkins goes to Al Hilal, while Liam Delap is edging closer to joining Nottingham Forest.

Chelsea no longer see Leeds as a loan destination for Mykhailo Mudryk, amid interest from sister club Strasbourg, while Hull want Dario Essugo but Strasbourg could also be a destination for the young midfielder.

Tosin has multiple interest from abroad and fellow centre-back Axel Disasi is close to signing for Crystal Palace.

Coventry

Coventry are hoping to wrap up their summer business with two more signings before they are next in Premier League action against fellow promoted side Hull City on Saturday.

They want to bring in a left-back and a centre-back before the deadline, having already added 10 players to Frank Lampard's squad in the hope of securing Premier League survival.

Coventry have already agreed a deal with Brentford to sign Ethan Pinnock. The centre-back is expected to have a medical this week ahead of completing a transfer understood to be worth up to £6m.

Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace are set to complete the signing of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea as a replacement for Maxence Lacroix but are yet to find a successor to Marc Guehi and could sign another centre-back.

Palace have been exploring options to reinforce out wide. Free agent Solly March is one they have been working towards after his Brighton exit.

There are question marks over three of Palace's most key players, Daniel Munoz, Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr, in the final week.

Sarr has reported interest from Galatasaray, but suggestions the winger is refusing to train are wide of the mark. He is currently injured.

Aston Villa have made an approach for Mateta, who has entered the final year of his deal. He was close to leaving six months ago for AC Milan. Munoz has interest from a number of clubs, including Everton.

Everton

David Moyes still wants a right-back and a potential change among his centre-forwards, as well as maybe another winger.

He wants Strasbourg's Guela Doue but the price is prohibitive, while others he likes are RB Leipzig's Ridle Baku and Crystal Palace's Daniel Munoz.

Everton face a similar situation with Liam Delap, but Nottingham Forest are currently ahead of them in the race to sign the Chelsea striker. Beto has interest from Fiorentina so it remains to be seen if some movement happens there.

There is still a chance Jack Grealish returns after his loan spell last season but he was in Manchester City's squad at the weekend as they try to get more bodies in themselves.

Fulham

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has said he wants more business to be done as he looks to bring balance to his squad. They seem to be prioritising a new right-back at the moment while they are yet to replace Harry Wilson and Issa Diop with a new winger or centre-back.

Talks have been held with Rennes over a deal for 20-year-old Morocco international centre-back Abdelhamid Ait-Boudlal but the French club appear reluctant to sell.

Summer signing Gonzalo Garcia appears to be Arbeloa's favoured striker, so will the returning Rodrigo Muniz be happy with that, or does there need to be a change among the back-up strikers? Let's see.

Hull

Hull City are expecting to be busy in the final week of the window and are looking to bring in at least five more players before the deadline.

The promoted side are close to reaching an agreement to sign centre-forward Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin and they are in talks with Deportivo La Coruna for winger Yeremay Hernandez.

Hull are also putting the finishing touches to an agreement with Nice for forward Mohamed-Ali Cho in a deal worth in the region of £15m and are still in the race to sign Stoke winger Sorba Thomas. Meanwhile, they have an interest in Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo, too.

Several squad players could leave the MKM Stadium before September 1.

Ipswich

Ipswich remain in talks with Bayer Leverkusen over a deal for midfielder Exequiel Palacios, after a bid was rejected last week.

They are looking to strengthen further in attack and midfield, with options also being explored for more depth at centre-forward. Ipswich are thought to be one of the clubs who like Burnley's Zian Flemming.

Sheffield Wednesday have agreed a straight loan deal with Ipswich to sign striker Ali Al-Hamadi. He is one of several players that could leave before the deadline and could mean another forward option is brought into Portman Road.

Wrexham are in talks to sign Anis Mehmeti, while Chiedozie Ogbene, Cameron Humphreys and Alex Palmer also have interest from elsewhere.

Leeds

Leeds will only do more if they can genuinely improve Daniel Farke's squad.

Checks have been made on Conrad Harder's availability at RB Leipzig, but club sources are playing down the chances of adding a striker.

Their strong interest in Mykhailo Mudryk remains despite doubts around Chelsea's willingness to do a deal with Leeds amid interest from Strasbourg.

Gabriel Gudmundsson's injury has highlighted the need for Leeds to sign full-back cover. As things stand, that also looks difficult to do.

Leeds are lining up Eintracht Frankfurt's Michael Zetterer to be the back-up goalkeeper, but a deal cannot proceed until Frankfurt land a new No 1. If Zetterer comes in, Lucas Perri can go to Torino.

Meanwhile, Mateo Joseph and Largie Ramazani are searching for new clubs.

Liverpool

Liverpool's priority, as it has been throughout the summer, is still to reinforce in wide areas.

They have been pursuing PSG duo Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye, while Brighton have also rejected two Liverpool offers for Yankuba Minteh, the latest being £60m.

PSG's valuation of £145m has been a stumbling block but Liverpool are currently the only club chasing the forward, who has entered the final two years of his deal and has grown dissatisfied with his role in the team.

Liverpool do not want to sell Cody Gakpo amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and would likely need two new wingers in before considering letting the Dutchman go.

Man City

Manchester City look like being one of the busiest clubs, in and out. Savio has joined Tottenham and Omar Marmoush is likely to follow if City can get bodies in the door. Palmeiras winger Allan is on his way over, while they also like Spurs target Cody Gakpo at Liverpool.

With another midfielder in Nico Gonzalez getting closer to Newcastle, City will sign a replacement and are interested in Enzo Fernandez, Alex Scott and Manu Kone.

City have been after a back-up striker all summer with interest in Junior Kroupi, but he is out injured until around October.

Man Utd

Manchester United are still on the search for a left-back but will only act if the right player becomes available. It is possible Carlos Baleba could be the club's last signing of the window.

As it stands, potential deals for Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly look unlikely. Alejandro Balde has been mooted as an option with Barcelona willing to let him go. United are aware of his situation but have not actively been pursuing him.

United could wait until next summer to pursue their defensive targets rather than look for a stopgap option as they did with the midfield a year ago.

Further incomings are unlikely. Interest from Italy for Joshua Zirkzee has not progressed and he is currently likely to stay, as is Marcus Rashford, who was given the club's No 9 shirt for the season.

Newcastle

Newcastle are working on potentially signing a midfielder, wide forward and a striker before the window closes.

A deal to sign Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City is understood to be advancing and there is hope an agreement can be struck this week with head coach Matthias Jaissle keen to add experience in the midfield.

Joe Willock's impressive performance in the 2-2 draw against Liverpool could see him stay at Newcastle in this window despite strong interest from Besiktas.

Nick Pope could depart with his replacements already through the door, while Jacob Murphy also has interest from Everton.

Nottingham Forest

Nottingham Forest are working hard to bring in Liam Delap from Chelsea to improve their striking options following Taiwo Awoniyi's £9m move to Coventry.

They have been pursuing Lucas Bergvall as an Elliot Anderson replacement, but Roberto De Zerbi insists he is staying at Spurs.

Forest could also add a right wing-back with Dodo at Fiorentina a player of interest.

Dilane Bakwa is set to join Lille on loan, while centre-backs Zach Abbott and Tyler Bindon could also depart on temporary moves amid interest from Watford.

Sunderland

Sunderland are expected to be busy and could bring in three more signings with a centre-back, winger and striker on the agenda.

They are keen on Sporting winger Geny Catamo, but that would likely be an expensive deal to do.

Jason Seelt is likely to go out on loan once a new contract is agreed. Udinese have been in contact with Sunderland, while Monza are also keen along with clubs in the Championship and Bundesliga.

Tottenham

Tottenham have spent north of £300m but still hope to sign two more forward players.

Spurs are close to agreeing a deal to sign Omar Marmoush from Man City and are also interested in Liverpool's Cody Gakpo. Pedro Neto is an alternative target but he is valued at close to £100m by Chelsea.

Spurs could see Pape Matar Sarr and Richarlison depart before the window closes, while Lucas Bergvall is now expected to stay at Spurs, according to Roberto De Zerbi.

articles.title: What are the key dates for the 2026-27 women's football season?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team details the key dates are for the 2026-27 women's football season.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 women's football season is under way, with the qualifying rounds of the Champions League already ongoing, as well as the Women's Africa Cup of Nations.

Later this month, the preliminary rounds of the FA Cup begin before the league campaigns of the Women's Super League and Women's Super League 2 start in early September.

The Subway Players Cup, also known as the League Cup, also gets under way in September, with the full rounds of the FA Cup starting at the end of October.

There will also be five international breaks during the season ahead of the 2027 Women's World Cup, which takes place across June and July in Brazil.

What are the key Women's Super League and Women's Super League 2 dates?

Friday, 4 September, 2026 â First game of the season

Monday, 21 December 2026 to Saturday, 3 January, 2027 â Winter break

Saturday, 22 May, 2027 â Last game of regular season

Saturday, 29 or Sunday, 30 May, 2027 â Promotion/relegation play-off

Saturday, 8/Sunday, 9 May, 2027 â Last game of regular season

Saturday, 22 or Sunday, 23, 2027 â Play-off pre-qualifying match

When is the FA Cup and Subway Players Cup?

Sunday, 23 August, 2026 â Preliminary round

Sunday, 6 September, 2026 â First qualifying round

Sunday, 20 September, 2026 â Second qualifying round

Sunday, 4 October, 2026 â Third qualifying round

Sunday, 25 October, 2026 â First round

articles.title: Leicester City: Premier League title moments - a decade on
articles.summary: Leicester are gearing up for League One but 10 years ago they were defending Premier League champions. The dream moments haven't been forgotten.
articles.body:
It was a dream then, it is a dream now - especially as Leicester prepare for League One.

Ten years ago the Foxes were preparing to defend their Premier League title and looking forward to Champions League football.

At 5,000-1, they had pulled off the most improbable, the most stunning, the most incredible feat to shock the world.

But now, after back-to-back relegations, those days seem almost as surreal as when they actually happened.

New manager Russell Martin will be expected to take the club back to the Championship at the first attempt, something that sounds nowhere near as impossible as what the Foxes previously managed.

A decade on, the 'pinch-me' moments live on for those who were there, and some have shared them with BBC Sport.

Spoiler: they might not be the ones you knew about.

Leicester had won the title without kicking a ball on 2 May 2016 when nearest challengers Tottenham Hotspur could only manage a 2-2 draw with Chelsea .

The next day, there was only one group of men the media wanted to speak to.

Crowds gathered at the club's former training ground at Belvoir Drive, a few miles outside the centre of Leicester.

Journalists and fans waited - one cameraman persuaded a neighbour to allow him in to film from their bathroom window as he aimed to get footage of the celebrating Foxes.

The media were finally instructed to head to King Power Stadium where the press room would be opened.

A five-minute drive took 30 minutes through revelling fans and it was a battle to get to there but, inside, the world's media edged in, hoping to hear from those who made this miracle possible.

But only eight reporters would receive a secret invitation to head back to Belvoir Drive.

Quietly, one-by-one, the handpicked members of the British press who regularly covered the club, slipped out of the packed room and made their way back.

This time, they were let in and ushered into the family room, just to the right of reception.

When manager Claudio Ranieri walked in, he received an immediate, impromptu, standing ovation and shook hands with those who had watched the astounding season unfold.

The man the world wanted to speak to gave an engaging audience to a few writers for 45 minutes.

Ranieri had been a left-field appointment at the start of that season, having not managed in England for 12 years since leaving Chelsea in 2004.

And he had considered bringing in some unconventional methods, such as double training sessions, which were nipped in the bud with the help of Craig Shakespeare, who had stayed on as assistant after the sacking of Ranieri's predecessor Nigel Pearson.

There were off-field changes he would bring in, though, including taking the squad out to make their own pizza after the first clean sheet of the season against Crystal Palace in October 2015.

"It sounds funny - we're keeping a clean sheet and gone for pizza but you then end up speaking to someone in the squad you probably wouldn't have spoken to at training because there's 25 of you," says former centre-back Robert Huth.

"You train, but you don't really know the guy. How's he functioning? Does he like me to shout at him? Does he want me to just be quiet?

"You talk and go through the game where maybe you wouldn't mention things, like a problem that you see on a pitch, if it's like, a stiff environment.

"If you're out and about, and you go: 'When the ball's here, I prefer if you do this' - just like tiny little things and you take criticism on differently when you talk in a social environment. You don't want to sit in a meeting room being told what to do."

It allowed winger Riyad Mahrez to flourish and Jamie Vardy to plunder 24 league goals, with Ranieri comparing his counter-attacking forwards to the RAF.

It is well documented that Vardy had invited the squad to his house to watch what would end up being the title-winning match as Spurs blew a 2-0 lead to draw with Chelsea - and that some players needed to wait at the local police station before arriving because of the crowds of fans who had gathered outside.

While everyone else partied, winger Nathan Dyer had a different night, in hospital with wife Laura after the birth of their second child, Shea, two days earlier.

"I had the laptop out watching the game in hospital, the boys were at the party. I wasn't able to make it but I'd never miss the birth of my child," he says.

"It was a strange feeling. It was surreal, like it wasn't real at the time but it was.

"We had to be put in a room as people were putting their heads round and even then you could see the eyes at the door. People were congratulating me and were really proud.

"It was the whole city, even people who were not fans were so happy Leicester had achieved this."

He'd had a dramatic arrival at the club in the first place that season, joining on loan from Swansea on transfer deadline day and being flown to Leicester in the late former owner Khun Vichai's helicopter to beat the deadline.

"My wife was pregnant, we'd just moved into a new house, so everything was in boxes, it was a wild day," he says.

"It was exciting for me but also nerve-wracking because it was so intense, to send the helicopter to get me to get it over the line. It was a proud moment for me - I'd always wanted to be involved in a moment like that, watching on the TV - breaking news!"

Leicester were two points behind Arsenal at the turn of the year but one defeat in the final 16 games - a dramatic late loss at Arsenal in February - had put them on course for the title.

The closer they edged to the impossible, the more the interest in the Foxes exploded.

Vardy had a lookalike - postman Lee Chapman - and Ranieri had a sausage named after him.

Local butchers W Archer & Son created the Ranieri from Packington free-range pork, fennel, garlic and chilli.

It won a star at the Great Taste awards and at one stage the shop was shifting 12kg (26.5lb) a day.

Owner Sean Jeynes even brought a plate of sausages to the stadium before a news conference, which led Ranieri to declare himself 'the sausageman'.

"It was surreal that day. How did that ever happen?" says Jeynes.

"We were making sausages two or three times a day, smelling of garlic, smelling of fennel, but it was just a crazy time. It really was a crazy time - you can't quite comprehend what it was like.

"It had a massive effect on the city, it had a great effect on everybody. Everyone was much happier.

"Nothing can replace the Italian sausage, the recipe, and the pork, fennel, garlic chili and a hint of Champions League.

"People would say, why don't you do a [Brendan] Rodgers sausage [after winning the FA Cup in 2021], but it's just not the same."

The sausage is still occasionally back on their counters, a lasting reminder of a unique time.

That is not the only taste of success that is still being enjoyed today.

"Thanks to Leicester City it meant I could retire at 55 instead of 67," says Foxes Trust co-chair Lynn Wyeth, who stuck Â£2 on the club at odds of 5,000-1 at the start of the season.

"It was actually really stressful. A first world problem, isn't it? It was stressful enough, watching them get closer and closer thinking, oh my god, can we do it? But knowing that there was Â£10,000 riding on it as well, was like, 'oh, no, I almost wish I'd cashed out earlier'.

"When I won, I had my account shut for money laundering, I had to prove it was me and that I'd won it.

"We managed to clear it up quite quickly, I think it's just an automatic thing.

Quietly, one-by-one, the handpicked members of the British press who regularly covered the club, slipped out of the packed room and made their way back.
This time, they were let in and ushered into the family room, just to the right of reception.
When manager Claudio Ranieri walked in, he received an immediate, impromptu, standing ovation and shook hands with those who had watched the astounding season unfold.
The man the world wanted to speak to gave an engaging audience to a few writers for 45 minutes.
Ranieri had been a left-field appointment at the start of that season, having not managed in England for 12 years since leaving Chelsea in 2004.

And he had considered bringing in some unconventional methods, such as double training sessions, which were nipped in the bud with the help of Craig Shakespeare, who had stayed on as assistant after the sacking of Ranieri's predecessor Nigel Pearson.
There were off-field changes he would bring in, though, including taking the squad out to make their own pizza after the first clean sheet of the season against Crystal Palace in October 2015.

"It sounds funny - we're keeping a clean sheet and gone for pizza but you then end up speaking to someone in the squad you probably wouldn't have spoken to at training because there's 25 of you," says former centre-back Robert Huth.
"You train, but you don't really know the guy. How's he functioning? Does he like me to shout at him? Does he want me to just be quiet?
"You talk and go through the game where maybe you wouldn't mention things, like a problem that you see on a pitch, if it's like, a stiff environment.

"If you're out and about, and you go: 'When the ball's here, I prefer if you do this' - just like tiny little things and you take criticism on differently when you talk in a social environment. You don't want to sit in a meeting room being told what to do."
It allowed winger Riyad Mahrez to flourish and Jamie Vardy to plunder 24 league goals, with Ranieri comparing his counter-attacking forwards to the RAF.

It is well documented that Vardy had invited the squad to his house to watch what would end up being the title-winning match as Spurs blew a 2-0 lead to draw with Chelsea - and that some players needed to wait at the local police station before arriving because of the crowds of fans who had gathered outside.
While everyone else partied, winger Nathan Dyer had a different night, in hospital with wife Laura after the birth of their second child, Shea, two days earlier.
"I had the laptop out watching the game in hospital, the boys were at the party. I wasn't able to make it but I'd never miss the birth of my child," he says.
"It was a strange feeling. It was surreal, like it wasn't real at the time but it was.
"We had to be put in a room as people were putting their heads round and even then you could see the eyes at the door. People were congratulating me and were really proud.
"It was the whole city, even people who were not fans were so happy Leicester had achieved this."

He'd had a dramatic arrival at the club in the first place that season, joining on loan from Swansea on transfer deadline day and being flown to Leicester in the late former owner Khun Vichai's helicopter to beat the deadline.
"My wife was pregnant, we'd just moved into a new house, so everything was in boxes, it was a wild day," he says.

"It was exciting for me but also nerve-wracking because it was so intense, to send the helicopter to get me to get it over the line. It was a proud moment for me - I'd always wanted to be involved in a moment like that, watching on the TV - breaking news!"
Leicester were two points behind Arsenal at the turn of the year but one defeat in the final 16 games - a dramatic late loss at Arsenal in February - had put them on course for the title.
The closer they edged to the impossible, the more the interest in the Foxes exploded.
Vardy had a lookalike - postman Lee Chapman - and Ranieri had a sausage named after him.
Local butchers W Archer & Son created the Ranieri from Packington free-range pork, fennel, garlic and chilli.
It won a star at the Great Taste awards and at one stage the shop was shifting 12kg (26.5lb) a day.
Owner Sean Jeynes even brought a plate of sausages to the stadium before a news conference, which led Ranieri to declare himself 'the sausageman'.
"It was surreal that day. How did that ever happen?" says Jeynes.
"We were making sausages two or three times a day, smelling of garlic, smelling of fennel, but it was just a crazy time. It really was a crazy time - you can't quite comprehend what it was like.
"It had a massive effect on the city, it had a great effect on everybody. Everyone was much happier.
"Nothing can replace the Italian sausage, the recipe, and the pork, fennel, garlic chili and a hint of Champions League.
"People would say, why don't you do a [Brendan] Rodgers sausage [after winning the FA Cup in 2021], but it's just not the same."
The sausage is still occasionally back on their counters, a lasting reminder of a unique time.
That is not the only taste of success that is still being enjoyed today.
"Thanks to Leicester City it meant I could retire at 55 instead of 67," says Foxes Trust co-chair Lynn Wyeth, who stuck Â£2 on the club at odds of 5,000-1 at the start of the season.

"It was actually really stressful. A first world problem, isn't it? It was stressful enough, watching them get closer and closer thinking, oh my god, can we do it? But knowing that there was Â£10,000 riding on it as well, was like, 'oh, no, I almost wish I'd cashed out earlier'.
"When I won, I had my account shut for money laundering, I had to prove it was me and that I'd won it.
"We managed to clear it up quite quickly, I think it's just an automatic thing.

articles.title: LSU Goalie Rylie Kuyper Rings the Bell in Emotional Video After Completing Chemotherapy Treatment
articles.summary: LSU goalie Rylie Kuyper finished her chemotherapy treatment for Stage 2 Hodgkin's lymphoma.
articles.body:
LSU goalie Rylie Kuyper finished her chemotherapy treatment for Stage 2 Hodgkin's lymphoma.

Our Lady of the Lake Cancer Institute posted an emotional video of Kuyper celebrating the milestone by ringing the bell with her entire team there to embrace her:

"Every ring represents a journey and a reminder that no one has to face cancer alone," the Instagram message read. " … We're honored to celebrate Rylie and continue supporting her on her healthcare journey."

Kuyper was previously at Texas Tech and is listed as a redshirt freshman on LSU's website .

The Tigers are 1-1 on the season with a victory over Northwestern State in their latest game. Next up is a matchup against UCF on Thursday.

articles.title: Deputy Tried to Serve Civil Papers to Deion Sanders at Colorado Practice, but Coach Was Unavailable
articles.summary: A deputy with the Boulder County Sheriff's Office showed up at the University of Colorado campus last week to serve civil papers to Deion Sanders while the coach was at an open practice and inaccessible.
articles.body:
A deputy with the Boulder County Sheriff's Office showed up at the University of Colorado campus last week to serve civil papers to Deion Sanders while the coach was at an open practice and inaccessible.

The officer was informed that the Buffaloes coach was "unavailable at the time to receive receipt of the papers," a spokesperson with the sheriff's office said Wednesday. Sanders is being subpoenaed to testify as part of a bankruptcy trial involving his son, Shilo, that begins on Aug. 31, according to USA Today.

The Colorado athletic department had no additional information. The Buffaloes open the season on Sept. 3 at Georgia Tech.

The deputy arrived on campus at 10:22 a.m. on Aug. 11 with civil papers. It was the day the Buffaloes held an open practice with specific rules in place that nothing observed could be reported, published or shared.

Carrie Haverfield, a senior communications specialist for the sheriff's office, wrote in an email to The Associated Press that it's not uncommon for civil papers to take several attempts to serve.

"While working with university staff to find a better time to complete the process, we heard from Mr. Sanders' legal counsel who indicated that they were able to receive receipt of the papers on behalf of Mr. Sanders, however, they were not located in Boulder County, so we transferred the paperwork to Denver to be served," Haverfield wrote. "We did not find any university staff to be attempting to block the civil service, on the contrary, they were attempting to help our deputy find a better time to do so. We do not disclose the specific contents of civil papers that we serve."

Shilo Sanders remains in litigation over a lawsuit stemming from an incident with a security guard when he was in high school. The guard filed a lawsuit against Sanders and was issued a default judgment when Sanders didn't show for his court date.

The hard-hitting safety who played for his dad at Colorado was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last August.

articles.title: Alabama, Tennessee Reportedly Set to Renew Historic Uniform Matchup for 2026, 2027 SEC Games
articles.summary: Alabama and Tennessee are reportedly planning to revive a longstanding tradition in their historic rivalry.
articles.body:
Alabama and Tennessee are reportedly planning to revive a longstanding tradition in their historic rivalry.

According to ESPN's Pete Thamel, the Crimson Tide and the Vols will both wear their home jerseys during their SEC matchups in 2026 and 2027. It will be the first time since 1970 that they will wear Alabama crimson and Tennessee orange in their rivalry game.

The rivalry between Alabama and Tennessee dates back over a century, with the Crimson Tide leading the all-time series 60-40-8. Still, the Vols' 40 wins are the most victories over Alabama of any program in college football.

The two teams have traded wins in each of the last four seasons, with Alabama taking home a 37-20 victory in 2025. They will meet on Oct. 17 this year.

articles.title: MLS Fight in Trending Video Leads to Red Card for 16-Year-Old Cavan Sullivan
articles.summary: A fight broke out near the end of a 2-2 draw between the Philadelphia Union and Inter Miami on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
A fight broke out near the end of a 2-2 draw between the Philadelphia Union and Inter Miami on Wednesday night.

Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan and Miami's Yannick Bright both received red cards for a scuffle that started after Sullivan's brother, Quinn, was taken down inside the box.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

Cavan is 16 years old, previously making MLS history as the youngest player to ever appear in a game as a 14-year-old during the 2024 season.

Now, the red card will force him to miss Philadelphia's clash with Austin FC on Saturday.

Bright also won't be available to suit up for Miami's Saturday matchup with Toronto FC.

Cavan's upcoming absence is a particularly tough blow to a Union squad that has relied on him as a consistent starter under interim manager Ryan Richter.

In 18 matches this year, Sullivan has picked up one goal and seven assists. He's been particularly sharp as of late, recording three assists in his past three appearances heading into Wednesday's action.

As for Bright, he's tallied three assists in 16 matches during his 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Texas Tech Unveils New Patrick Mahomes-Branded Adidas Uniforms in Video for 2026 CFB Season
articles.summary: Texas Tech football is introducing a third edition of Patrick Mahomes-inspired uniforms ahead of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Texas Tech football is introducing a third edition of Patrick Mahomes-inspired uniforms ahead of the 2026 college football season.

The Red Raiders revealed a first look Thursday at the team's new "Let's Ride" uniform in collaboration with Adidas and the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback.

The red and black uniforms feature Mahomes' signature "Gladiator" logo as well as his name on the back of the helmet.

Texas Tech will wear the new uniforms Sept. 18 for a Week 3 home game against Houston.

The Red Raiders first debuted uniforms featuring Mahomes' logo with their "Mahomes Strategy" look ahead of the 2024 season.

Texas Tech once more collaborated with Mahomes last season for the team's "Too Cold" look , which also featured the Gladiator logo.

Mahomes' uniform designs have also extended beyond Texas Tech. He and Adidas recently gave gear inspired by the Red Raiders' "Too Cold" uniforms to 28 high schools ahead of the 2026-27 academic year.

articles.title: Henrik Sedin's Son Valter Agrees to Contract with MLS' Whitecaps NEXT Pro Team
articles.summary: The son of Vancouver Canucks legend Henrik Sedin is returning to the Vancouver Whitecaps.
articles.body:
The son of Vancouver Canucks legend Henrik Sedin is returning to the Vancouver Whitecaps.

The club announced Thursday that Valter Sedin signed a contract with Whitecaps 2, which competes in the MLS NEXT Pro developmental league.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

"I'm excited to be back at the club and to sign a professional contract," he said. "I'm looking forward to continuing to develop my game, and to continue pushing forward in my career."

Sedin joined the Whitecaps youth academy in 2020 but left in 2025 to sign with the under-19 side for Swedish club Hammarby.

Most recently, the 19-year-old represented Canada in the Concacaf U-20 Championship. He scored a goal in the 56th minute of the 2-2 draw with Jamaica to close out the group stage.

Canada advanced to the semifinals and in doing so earned a spot in the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup.

While Sedin is signed to Whitecaps 2, he's eligible to be called up to Vancouver's senior squad on a short-term basis if the need arises. In the meantime, he'll get to continue refining his game.

articles.title: Utah Sues Freddie Whittingham for Breach of Contract After He Joined His Brother at Michigan
articles.summary: SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — The University of Utah is suing former assistant coach Freddie Whittingham for breach of contract after he left to join his brother Kyle's staff at Michigan.
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — The University of Utah is suing former assistant coach Freddie Whittingham for breach of contract after he left to join his brother Kyle's staff at Michigan.

The lawsuit filed in Utah's Third District Court is seeking more than $300,000 for breach of contract and at least $1 million for general and special damages.

The lawsuit contends Whittingham abandoned his roll as Utah's tight ends coach to take the same job at Michigan despite being under contract through January 2027. It alleges Whittingham failed to provide written notice of resignation, get written consent from Utah to speak with Michigan and pay liquidation damages specified under terms of the contract.

The lawsuit also claims Whittingham failed to devote full-time attention and energy to his duties at Utah and that he actively recruited Utah players to Michigan while still employed by the school.

Kyle Whittingham coached at Utah for 21 years and was the winningest coach in school history before stepping down last fall. Michigan hired him two weeks later to replace the fired Sherrone Moore.

Freddie Whittingham had been a part of his brother's staff at Utah for 14 years.

articles.title: Nick Saban Reacts to Mario Cristobal's 'ACC Bulls--t' in Funny Video on CFB Conference Debate
articles.summary: College football coaching legend Nick Saban jokingly called out Miami head coach Mario Cristobal for attempting to convince him that the ACC is better than the SEC.
articles.body:
College football coaching legend Nick Saban jokingly called out Miami head coach Mario Cristobal for attempting to convince him that the ACC is better than the SEC.

"This guy is the best salesman in the history of ball," Saban said during a Friday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:11 mark). "He's a great recruiter but if he ever gets fired, he'll be the best used car salesman in south Florida. I guarantee, no doubt. He calls me up with this ACC bulls--t."

"He's always trying to convince me that the ACC's better than the SEC," he added. "The SEC has nine teams in the top 25. That's all I know. It's a deep conference. It just is. I know that the Big Ten is a really good conference and getting better when it comes to depth, but really good at the top with Ohio State and Oregon. But anyway, it is what it is. He's never going to convince me, never, that the ACC is better than the SEC."

While Cristobal and Miami couldn't capture the ACC title last season, they still compiled a 13-3 record and advanced to the College Football Playoff national championship game.

The Hurricanes were ultimately defeated by Indiana, the Big Ten champions.

As for Saban, his 17 seasons at Alabama were highlighted by six national titles and nine SEC championships.

Cristobal was previously a member of Saban's coaching staff on the Crimson Tide, operating in several roles with the school from 2013-16.

Miami is entering the 2026 season attempting to become the first ACC team to win the CFP since Clemson in 2018.

articles.title: Alabama Names QB1 After Keelon Russell vs. Austin Mack Battle, New Rumors Reveal Ahead of CFB Season
articles.summary: Alabama's offense will be led by sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell to start the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Alabama's offense will be led by sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell to start the 2026 season.

Per ESPN's Pete Thamel , Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer is going with Russell over Austin Mack after the two competed for the starting job throughout camp.

Russell and Mack both played behind Ty Simpson last season. Mack received more playing time in 2025, appearing in four games and attempting 32 passes. Russell had 15 pass attempts in two games.

Speaking to reporters in July about the quarterback competition, DeBoer expressed confidence in both players being able to run the offense at a high level:

"Our quarterbacks do have the belief and trust amongst our entire team. There are different ways where I've seen that, whether it was in the spring or through the summer. There are different conversations, different activities that we do where I really can get a good feel of it being genuine, that our team trusts that whoever steps on the football field and takes those snaps is going to be a guy — and I think that's because they believe in both guys."

Russell arrived in Tuscaloosa last year with tremendous hype. He was a 5-star prospect and No. 2 overall recruit in the 2025 class, behind only Bryce Underwood.

Even though Russell had very limited playing time during his freshman season, there is plenty of belief from talent evaluators around the country in his ability to become a star quickly.

"He's got a lot of ability," an SEC general manager told The Athletic's Antonio Morales and Sam Khan Jr. about Russell. "We just haven't seen it on the big stage yet."

Mack, a 4-star recruit in the 2023 class, started his college career at Washington with DeBoer. He redshirted in his first season with the Huskies before transferring to Alabama after DeBoer was hired following Nick Saban's retirement.

The 20-year-old Mack has appeared in five games over the past two seasons. He is 26-of-35 for 267 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

Alabama is starting the season ranked No. 13 in the Associated Press Preseason Top 25 poll. It's the first time the program has been outside the top 10 in the AP preseason poll since 2008 when Saban was entering his second year as head coach.

The Crimson Tide will kickoff the 2026 season against East Carolina at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Sept. 5.

articles.title: Mou sorprende y alumbra una nueva sociedad
articles.standfirst: Bellingham y Güler jugaron juntos de inicio y fabricaron el primer gol del nuevo Real Madrid
articles.summary: Bellingham y Güler jugaron juntos de inicio y fabricaron el primer gol del nuevo Real Madrid
articles.body: Uno de los grandes alicientes del partido de este sábado era conocer el primer once inicial de José Mourinho en su segunda etapa en el Real Madrid. Había expectación y casi una ‘certeza’. Parecía improbable que Jude Bellingham y Arda Güler compartieran lugar en el once, pero eso fue justamente lo que sucedió. Mou no movió de su sitio a Bellingham, al que reserva el papel de llegador en el que deslumbró en el pasado Mundial. El que se desplazó de su habitual zona de influencia fue Güler, al que el entrenador del Madrid colocó como falso extremo derecho. En realidad, el internacional turco fue el arquitecto de la mayor parte del juego ofensivo del Real Madrid, con Bernardo Silva más cerca de la base y menos contacto con el balón que el turco. De hecho, la sociedad Güler-Bellingham abrió el marcador para lo que acabó siendo una sufridísima victoria del Madrid gracias al gol de Espí en el 90’. El partido parecía encaminado a un desarrollo muy diferente cuando Arda sacó el guante en una falta desde el costado izquierdo del ataque blanco. El centro del turco, con música, culminó en un frentazo colocado de Bellingham para hacer el primer gol del Madrid en el minuto 9. Era el justo premio a la buena salida de los blancos, que hasta el minuto 20, más o menos, pasaron por encima de su rival, al que permitieron respirar hacia la mitad de la primera parte. El Espanyol reaccionó logrando el gol del empate y llevando el partido sin decidir hasta literalmente el último minuto, cuando Espí mandó a la red el balón que dio al Madrid sus tres primeros puntos en la Liga 26-27. En la jugada del gol del delantero valenciano no participaron ni Güler ni Bellingham, que habían sido sustituidos antes por Mou. articles.title: Espí, el Barça y el Atleti
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Nunca conocí una Liga con un inicio tan cochambroso como el de esta, que ha arrancado partido a partido, como una fila de hormigas, con acumulaciones de encuentros fuera para algunos y en casa para otros, un mal y apresurado guiso cuyas causas son la decisión de Tebas por iniciarla a mediados de agosto (se estima en 40 millones el mayor ingreso de televisión al evitar que demasiados abonados a las plataformas no renueven hasta septiembre) y el apretón del Mundial, en el que por fortuna muchos de los jugadores de nuestro campeonato duraron bastante. A eso ha habido que sumar, en el caso del Atlético, el respeto a contratos del estadio para esos conciertos que ya no se hacen en el Bernabéu. Encima, y esto es mal común en toda Europa, las plantillas están sin cerrar hasta fin de mes, lo que da un aire como provisional a lo que hasta entonces veamos, sólo que será el definitivo enfado a los nostálgicos. Está, por ejemplo, el caso colgado de Julián Alvarez, con el que el Barça ha repetido el enredo de los dos veranos pasados con Nico Williams con la misma consecuencia: quedarse sin el jugador y dejar a este en posición incómoda ante sus aficionados. El Barça, que creyó contar con él, se apañó ayer con Raphinha en esa posición, pero está buscando delantero centro. Por su parte el Atlético, que tiene a Sorloth lesionado, ha tratado de apañarse con Lookman, que no conoce los parámetros del puesto. Ayer el Cholo tiró de Julián Alvarez, entre pitos y bronca, cuando las cosas estaban mal, y al chico se le vio ausente, triste, entre depre y desinteresado. Prácticamente no la tocó (¡qué bien le hubiera venido marcar el gol que hizo Giulano!) y ni siquiera fue al fondo al final del partido a despedirse, con todos, de la grada de animación. Medida prudente. El Barça trata de remediarse con Gyokeres, del Arsenal, y nadie está seguro de que el Atlético no pretenda lo mismo, en su caso utilizando a Julián Alvarez en la negociación. A él se le siguen notando pocas ganas de quedarse, incluso me dicen que su entorno se planteó litigar por ‘cláusula abusiva’ (son 500 millones), lo que no creo que tenga el menor recorrido. Los problemas de ambos clubes con el nueve resaltan el acierto del Madrid al ir por Carlos Espí, jugador de gran futuro que ya ha marcado dos goles en la pretemporada y uno más, en Cornellà, que valió dos puntos. Me pregunto por qué ni Barça ni Atlético se interesaron por él. Primer partido de la temporada y primera bronca y flamear de pañuelos en Mestalla. “¡Queremos un tiro a puerta…!” y “¿Dónde están los fichajes…?” fueron dos de los cánticos ante el insufrible partido del equipo, dejado de la mano de Dios. Lo único notable en torno a la plantilla es la oferta desastrosa de renovación que se le ha hecho al ‘capi’ Gayá, en realidad una invitación encubierta a marcharse. Nada mueve a la ilusión que el fútbol necesita. La Comunidad de Madrid se ha puesto el pantalón de cuadros con Martín Presa, y le ha erradicado de Vallecas para adecentar el campo. No se fue a Burgos, como amenazó de forma extravagante Martín Presa, sino a Leganés. Malo todo para el club, cuyo problema es que su propietario no es presidente del Rayo, sino de la primera plantilla del Rayo, lo único que le divierte y le interesa. Lo demás lo desprecia, lo ignora. Y se le pudre entre las manos.

articles.title: Asencio y un último intento
articles.standfirst: El central español supera el problema muscular, pero la tibia vuelve a golpear: último intento antes del quirófano
articles.summary: El central español supera el problema muscular, pero la tibia vuelve a golpear: último intento antes del quirófano
articles.body: Raúl Asencio se enfrenta a un último intento para evitar el quirófano. El central del Real Madrid ha superado ya la lesión que le ha tenido apartado esta temporada por un problema en el cuádriceps, pero la misma pierna vuelve a darle problemas. Esta vez, en la tibia. Una dolencia que arrastra desde la pasada campaña y que no terminó de cerrar como se esperaba. La situación obliga al jugador a iniciar un nuevo tratamiento. Asencio ya ha completado varias sesiones en Valdebebas con el objetivo de descargar y recuperar la zona afectada. Si la evolución no es la esperada, la alternativa será pasar por el quirófano y afrontar una baja estimada de entre seis y ocho semanas. El problema viene de lejos. La tibia ya condicionó la recta final de la pasada temporada, cuando las lesiones golpeaban con especial dureza a la plantilla del Real Madrid. En aquel momento, Asencio decidió no parar. El equipo necesitaba centrales y él dio un paso adelante pese a que el riesgo era evidente. "No paro ahora ni loco", llegó a decir cuando se le planteó la posibilidad de detenerse. Una decisión tan valiente como arriesgada, porque el jugador se jugó el físico en un momento en el que el equipo atravesaba una situación límite. La solución entonces fue buscar una vía intermedia que le permitiera seguir compitiendo. Asencio recibió un tratamiento mínimamente invasivo destinado a retirar células anómalas en la zona de la cicatriz de la tibia, donde se había formado un callo mal consolidado. La consolidación no era la adecuada y podía terminar debilitando el hueso hasta convertir la fisura en una fractura. El cuerpo médico apostó entonces por un tratamiento que permitiera ganar tiempo y evitar una operación inmediata. Asencio pudo seguir ayudando al equipo. Con el final de la temporada llegó el momento de descansar. El plan durante el verano era sencillo: reposo, recuperación y dejar que el paso del tiempo permitiera a la zona regenerarse. La previsión era que la tibia respondiera al descanso después de meses de exigencia. Pero no ha ocurrido así. La situación de Asencio ha empeorado y la tibia vuelve a convertirse en una amenaza para su temporada. El problema podría haberse visto agravado por la lesión en el cuádriceps, también en la misma pierna, que le ha obligado a modificar sus cargas y su trabajo durante la pretemporada. Ahora el jugador afronta un último intento antes de tomar una decisión mucho más drástica. El tratamiento ya está en marcha en Valdebebas y las primeras sesiones ya se han completado. El objetivo es descargar la zona y conseguir que responda sin necesidad de intervención quirúrgica. El margen, sin embargo, es reducido. Si el tratamiento no funciona, Asencio tendrá que pasar por el quirófano y estaría alrededor de dos meses fuera de combate. Un golpe especialmente duro para el central en el inicio de una temporada en la que Mourinho no puede contar con toda su defensa.

articles.title: Pep Chavarría, el "hijo ideal" que defenderá la izquierda de Xabi Alonso
articles.standfirst: En diez temporadas, el lateral ha pasado de jugar en Tercera a la Premier League
articles.summary: En diez temporadas, el lateral ha pasado de jugar en Tercera a la Premier League
articles.body: El fútbol puede dar muchas vueltas, si no que se lo pregunten a Pep Chavarría. De turnarse entre el mediocentro y el lateral en Tercera división con el equipo de su ciudad, a ser el carrilero izquierdo de un doble campeón de Champions League en la Premier League. "Por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche, soñaba con momentos como este. Cuando era niño, siempre fue mi objetivo llegar a un club así", contó el de Figueras en su presentación con el Chelsea. Pep Chavarría comenzó en el equipo de su ciudad, el UE Figueres donde ya confiaba en llegar a la élite del fútbol. "Cuando era pequeño, siempre le decía a mis amigos que iba a ser futbolista profesional. Al principio, solo jugaba por diversión, pero con el tiempo empecé a ver que realmente podía hacerlo", contó hace unos años en una entrevista con el medio La Razón.  Durante su etapa en el UE Figueres de Tercera división, el director deportivo del Olot, Sergi Raset, se fijó en él y se lo comentó a su entrenador en aquel momento, Raúl Garrido. "Me habló de un chico que creía que podía ser interesante, me pasó un par de vídeos... y le dije que sí". Comenta el actual director deportivo del SD Portmany a MARCA. Pep Chavarría dejó un gran recuerdo por su paso por el Olot. "Era un jugador muy completo, sobre todo a nivel ofensivo. Alternaba la posición de mediocentro con el carril, nosotros le adaptamos al carril con tres centrales", declara Raúl. Además por su rendimiento sobre el campo, el que fuera su míster, elogia su forma de ser. "Era un chico excelente, o sea, era el hijo ideal, el hermano perfecto, el novio ideal, digamos que era un chico con una educación excepcional, con unas ganas de aprender tremendas, escuchaba mucho, una humildad espectacular". Después del UE Olot, Pep fichó por el Zaragoza, a pesar de que se interesaron por él varios filiales. "Tenía claro que tenía el nivel para estar en Primera división", aclara Raúl. "Ha ido quemando etapas de una manera muy natural...Con su trabajo y con su rendimiento se ha ganado estar en el Chelsea por méritos propios porque me parece un jugador excepcional", finaliza. Después de dos temporadas en el Real Zaragoza donde se consolidó como uno de los mejores laterales izquierdos de la competición, Andoni Iraola le fichó para su Rayo de Primera división. Comenzó como suplente de Fran García y luego del Pacha Espino, pero a base de esfuerzo y oficio consiguió alcanzar el puesto de titular con Iñigo Pérez, su máximo valedor en Vallecas.  Esa buena relación que le llevó a mostrar su mejor versión sobre el campo, era recíproca. "Es el mejor entrenador que he tenido porque he aprendido mucho con él y con el 'staff' que tiene a su alrededor", afirmó Pep sobre Iñigo en una entrevista para RTVE. Con el conjunto rayista sumó 125 apariciones y fue indispensable para lograr esas cuatro últimas permanencias consecutivas y alcanzar la final de Leipzig. Después de esas noches inolvidables en Vallecas, Pep era uno de los jugadores con más cartel del club y el Chelsea vio en él un sustituto perfecto para Marc Cucurella. "Hablé con Xabi y me explicó sus ideas y cómo puedo encajar con ellas. Quiere mi intensidad, esos uno contra uno, mis desmarques de área a área, tanto en ataque como en defensa y así es como juego", declaró el jugador a los medios del club. Pep probará fortuna en una nueva liga después de consagrarse como uno de los mejores laterales españolas. Atrás quedaron los encuentros con sus amigos. Stamford Bridge le espera.

articles.title: Mourinho, a muerte con Vinicius
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués defendió al 7 del Madrid en público... y también en privado con una conversación en la que le quiso mostrar su confianza ciega
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués defendió al 7 del Madrid en público... y también en privado con una conversación en la que le quiso mostrar su confianza ciega
articles.body: Mourinho ha elegido bando. Y es el de Vinicius. El entrenador portugués no solo salió públicamente en defensa del brasileño después del partido contra el Espanyol. También habló con él en privado para trasladarle un mensaje inequívoco: Está y estará siempre con él. El crack brasileño, recién renovado por el Madrid, apenas ha empezado a trabajar con Mourinho en esta nueva etapa pero ya sabe que tiene al entrenador de su lado como escudo anti-balas. El partido de Cornellà no cambia esa consideración. Vinicius no tuvo su mejor noche, estuvo demasiado pendiente de los enfrentamientos con los rivales, recibió una amarilla y acabó entrando en una dinámica que Mourinho quiere ayudarle a controlar. Pero una actuación por debajo de lo esperado no altera la valoración del entrenador. Mucho menos después de un solo partido. El portugués entiende, además, que Vinicius necesita sentirse respaldado en un contexto en el que vuelve a estar en el centro de todas las miradas. Los abucheos, los silbidos y los insultos que recibió durante el encuentro contra el Espanyol fueron constantes y el técnico no quiso dejar pasar la oportunidad de defender públicamente a su jugador. “Vini no es un santo, pero lo que le hacen es demasiado”, dijo Mourinho. Y fue todavía más lejos al denunciar una situación que, a su juicio, se repite con el brasileño: “Tiene ya un formato, tiene algo que se repite entre adversarios. Primero le doy yo, ahora le das tú; ahora le doy yo, ahora le das tú. Si yo cojo una amarilla, le das tú. Salgo yo, que tengo amarilla, entra uno sin amarilla y le da. Es una frustración para él”. El portugués habló también de “bullying” desde las gradas y los rivales: “Estamos en una era social de antibullying, con Vini estamos todavía en el bullying del adversario y del público”. No fue una defensa destinada a justificar todo lo que haga el brasileño. Mourinho sabe que Vinicius tiene que controlar sus emociones y evitar que las provocaciones le aparten del partido. Pero una cosa es exigirle que mejore ese aspecto y otra muy diferente cuestionar su importancia. Mourinho no tiene ninguna duda sobre Vinicius. Y quiso que el futbolista lo supiera también en privado. Después de las críticas aparecidas tras el estreno liguero, el técnico habló con él para trasladarle tranquilidad y confianza. Para Mourinho, Vinicius es una pieza fundamental del equipo que está construyendo porque necesita futbolistas capaces de romper partidos. Extremos que no tengan miedo de recibir abiertos, encarar, atacar al lateral y obligar a toda una defensa a retroceder. En esa descripción encaja Vinicius a la perfección. Su movilidad libera espacios para Mbappé, Bellingham y el resto de los atacantes. Y su capacidad para jugar a campo abierto convierte cualquier recuperación en una amenaza. Pero hay algo más que Mourinho valora especialmente: el carácter. El técnico portugués quiere un Madrid competitivo, agresivo, ambicioso. Un equipo que no se conforme. Y entiende que Vinicius representa buena parte de ese ADN. Su personalidad, su hambre, su capacidad para asumir responsabilidad y su obsesión por ser decisivo forman parte de las características que Mourinho pretende potenciar, no apagar. Por eso el entrenador no interpreta el primer partido de Vini como una señal de alarma. Al contrario. Sabe que la temporada acaba de empezar, que el brasileño todavía tiene margen para mejorar físicamente y que su rendimiento irá creciendo conforme aumenten los minutos, la confianza y el entendimiento con sus compañeros. La cuestión, para Mourinho, no es si Vinicius va a ser importante. La cuestión es hasta dónde puede llevarlo. Una de las grandes misiones del portugués durante esta temporada será precisamente esa: maximizar las virtudes de sus futbolistas y conseguir que alcancen un nivel todavía superior. Y con Vini, el reto es especialmente atractivo.

articles.title: Roberto Gómez: "Lo que le ha hecho el Barcelona al Atlético no tiene nombre"
articles.standfirst: El periodista asegura en La Tribu que Julián Álvarez no se marchará del club rojiblanco salvo que llegue la cantidad exigida y señala directamente a Joan Laporta
articles.summary: El periodista asegura en La Tribu que Julián Álvarez no se marchará del club rojiblanco salvo que llegue la cantidad exigida y señala directamente a Joan Laporta
articles.body: La situación de Julián Álvarez centró buena parte de la intervención de Roberto Gómez en La Tribu, con Javi Amaro. Después de la fuerte pitada que recibió el argentino en el Metropolitano, el periodista mantuvo su postura sobre el futuro del delantero y cargó con dureza contra el Barcelona y Joan Laporta. Gómez reconoció la contundencia de la reacción de la grada con Julián: "Indudablemente es un sentir de la afición. El público no siempre tiene razón". Sobre la pitada recibida por el delantero, añadió: "Ayer se pita a un futbolista que sale en un momento determinado del encuentro. Una pitada brutal". Al final del encuentro, "el club decide, con muy buen criterio, que se retire y evita una situación comprometida". Pese a lo ocurrido, Roberto Gómez mantiene que el argentino continuará como rojiblanco: "No se va, y no se va a marchar del Atlético de Madrid, salvo que venga un equipo y ponga la cantidad que, indudablemente, tienen en su contrato". Además, descartó de manera tajante su llegada al conjunto azulgrana: "Desde luego, donde no va a ir es al FC Barcelona". Fue entonces cuando Gómez cargó contra la actuación del Barcelona: "Lo que ha hecho el Barcelona no tiene nombre en la historia del fútbol. O sea, la ofensa y el trato que ha dado el FC Barcelona al Atlético de Madrid es impresentable". Una crítica que dirigió especialmente hacia su presidente: "Sobre todo, y comenzando por el presidente, por Joan Laporta". El periodista cuestionó la forma de actuar del club azulgrana: "¿Qué te parece que el Barcelona y Laporta, cuyas relaciones con el Atlético de Madrid están rotas, haya asaltado con premeditación y alevosía la casa del Atlético de Madrid y no haya llamado al equipo rojiblanco?". Y terminó lanzando un mensaje directo a Laporta: "Que lo haga, que llame, y que escuche la respuesta de Enrique Cerezo". Roberto Gómez también puso el foco en Ceuta y reclamó una mayor presencia de Rafael Louzán. "¿Dónde está el presidente Louzán? El presidente de la selección campeona del mundo lleva un mes desaparecido", señaló. "El presidente de la Federación tiene que ir con el seleccionador a Ceuta", y aseguró que "a Luis de la Fuente le gustaría muchísimo ir con la Copa a Ceuta. La visita sería una inyección de moral para nuestros paisanos". Por último, el periodista fue muy crítico con el arbitraje en este inicio de temporada. Tras denunciar "una patada a Vinicius" que calificó como "una agresión", se refirió también a los penaltis señalados en el Metropolitano y especialmente al segundo: "El árbitro está a un metro y sale corriendo y no ve absolutamente nada, y para mí no es penalti". Su conclusión fue rotunda: "El nivel arbitral en estas primeras jornadas está siendo horroroso. Horroroso".

articles.title: Harry Kane wins a trophy with Bayern, Anthony Gordon makes his Barcelona debut plus lots more in the Euro Debrief
articles.summary: A trophy for Harry Kane with Bayern Munich and two assists for Anthony Gordon on his Barcelona debut; Adam Bate picks out the big stories from the continent in the Euro Debrief, a Sky Sports column focusing on the major European leagues and more
articles.body:
Welcome to The Euro Debrief, a new Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:

  • Kane bags another trophy with Bayern
  • Mourinho wins late while Gordon shines
  • Amorim's Milan win but Inter look strong
  • PSG start slowly compared to Marseille
  • Salah scores two in win for Trabzonspor

Kane wins Supercup with thanks to Brown

Being in Dortmund for the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup, the expectation was that Harry Kane would add to the 73 goals that he scored last season for Bayern Munich. Instead, the opener in their 2-1 win at Borussia Dortmund was scored by Nathaniel Brown.

The summer signing from Eintracht Frankfurt is better known as a left-back but was preferred in the No 10 role to fellow new arrival Ismael Saibari and responded by whipping the ball low into the corner inside the first half. He could have had more too.

Brown, 23, fired just wide of the far post after getting away down the left channel in the 43rd minute and drew roars from the away end when he charged forward just after the hour. He then sprang another attack with a smart turn that led to Kane firing just over.

Speaking to Kane afterwards, he praised his new partner. "It was a great performance. Not his natural position but he has had spells there in pre-season. He is obviously a smart player, really good on the ball, good in tight areas, and you saw that with his finish."

Kane described Brown as "a very versatile player" and pointed out that he had already scored in pre-season. But some adjustments will be required. Brown barely touched the ball prior to his 28th-minute goal, often being missed out of their passing sequences.

Vincent Kompany will have to be patient with Jamal Musiala following his unfortunate health scare, twice collapsing on the pitch. Saibari will be able to help with that. But the creative use of Brown could prove useful when the Bundesliga kicks off next weekend.
